purpose: Wing and part introductions for the entrance pages, written to be read or heard before a visitor chooses a room. Room order follows curation/exhibitions/structure/.

wings.title: Faces
introduction: One hundred and thirty-four faces, drawn between October 2021 and July 2022. They begin with a white box head on green and end with a collection piece that spells the artist's name across the square. Every one is a head, and almost every one has teeth. This is the wing where the mask is invented, and where it is first found out.

The six rooms are hung by what the faces are made of, and each one carries a different feeling. Heads built from boxes, which are toys and know it. Faces found in a tangle of scribble, which start as friends and end as snarls. Faces with weight and light, where for one winter the mask comes off and the people underneath are tired and kind. Skulls in the dark, which are fear drawn as a face. Sparer faces in line on flat color, where the teeth are a joke. And box heads with their eyes crossed out, blind and grinning, which end the wing on the artist's name.

The parts recur from room to room: the ringed eye, the spiral, the X, the grid of block teeth. What changes is how much of the square they are allowed to fill, and what the grin under them means. The artist has said the work was made to please the eye and flawed on purpose. The flaw is the grin: it never says whether it is pleased or about to bite, and the whole wing is built on not telling you. The Faces were drawn on Nifty Ink, a free drawing board that kept every stroke, and collected by one family in Minneapolis in the spring of 2022; both stories are told in the story pages.

wings.title: New Nifty on the Block
introduction: Three hundred and three works in ten months, from December 8, 2021 to October 15, 2022. It is the largest collection here, and it changes as it goes, so the wing is in three dated parts, each with its own rooms. The title is a joke about a boy band and a word for a neighborhood, and the wing is a year on that block: who lived there, what they wore on their faces, and what happened to the neighborhood while the drawings were being made.

The first part is figures and creatures: crowds of line, black silhouettes on bright color, skeletons, painted places, and the beams of May, drawn in the week the crypto market fell. The second is the mask summer, ten weeks of square, round and scribbled heads, drawn while the artist handed out cats to every holder and then announced that the year's inks would burn. The third is the August cats, a turn to portraits with tears on their cheeks, and the crowned masks that end on the three works of October 15, the last of them the collection piece. The crown on those last heads is the gallery's one open comparison in this wing: it is the crown Basquiat drew, and the artist never said so.

Every room is hung in the order the works were drawn, and the rooms say what the record says: the artist's posts that announced each work, often with a price, the gifts minted into collectors' wallets, and the purchases of the one collector who bought the series a drawing at a time from May and, on October 16, 2022, bought its origin piece and received the rest in a single afternoon. Read across the parts and the whole year is there: the line, then the mask, then the face. The grin stays the same throughout, and the wing is about what it was hiding.

parts.title: Figures and Creatures
introduction: The first six months. Whole figures and creatures, before the masks: crowds drawn as line, flat black animals ringed with wavy marks, bony skeletons dancing on color, soft painted places, and in May a run of heads whose eyes give off light. The block is new, everyone on it is a friend, and the drawings are the warmest in the series.

Six rooms. Start with the black silhouettes if you want the clearest formula, or with the line figures if you want to see the first drawing in the series. The skeleton room holds the collector's first purchase from the series, on May 1, 2022, and the beam room holds the week the market fell.

parts.title: Masks
introduction: Ten weeks in which nearly every drawing was a mask. Heads built as boxes inside boxes, heads drawn as rings and profiles, heads buried in scribble, and one room of what else was drawn in between: figures, crowds, a dog, a tree. The summer began with the artist giving drawings away and ended, on August 11, with the announcement that the year's inks would burn.

Four rooms. The parts of the mask are a kit, and each room is a different way of arranging it. The scribbled heads are the darkest; the room of what was drawn in between is where the artist, the day after deciding to burn, spent longer than on any other drawing putting leaves on a tree.

parts.title: Cats and Portraits
introduction: The last eight weeks. Two weeks of black cats in striped rooms, then flat creatures in one color each; heads that look like people, in hats, with worried eyes, five of them drawn on the day of the Ethereum Merge; and the last crowned masks, ending on the three works made on October 15, 2022, the last of them the collection piece.
Three rooms. The wing ends in Crowns and Last Masks, on #0000, which the collector bought the next morning for 750 xDai; the artist then sent the rest of the series to his wallet that afternoon.

wings.title: Rawblocks
introduction: Sixty-six works, nearly all from October 30, 2022 to March 15, 2023, with two masks from the May before. Portraits painted fast, patterned masks and flat black figures, heads in a few lines and heads in a storm of them, and a collection piece that crowds the whole series into one square.
Three rooms, and then a coda: the two landscapes painted in the hours after the collection piece, the only works in the series with no head in them. They close the wing.
wings.codaNote: Coda: Two Landscapes holds two works and is named as a coda, not a room.

wings.title: Abstract
introduction: Fifty-two works with no faces and no dates. The Abstract series comes from a different platform and carries no record of when each work was made, so the rooms follow the title numbers, which run from bands and washes toward thrown and swirled marks.
Two rooms. The first is bars, stripes, grids and washes, marks laid side by side until they make a surface. The second is splashes, scribbles and swirls, and it ends on the collection piece.

wings.title: Other nnxyz
introduction: Forty-five works outside the named series, from the first day on Nifty Ink in October 2021 to December 2024. Pieces made for occasions, milestones and summers; a few full figures and scenes; and the numbered masks of 2023 and 2024, denser and heavier than the earlier ones.
Two rooms. The first holds the occasions and figures, with one related item from Scrimshaw shown at its end. The second holds the masks.

wings.title: Scrimshaw
introduction: Twenty-five heads by Scrimshaw, a different artist who drew on Nifty Ink at the same time. They are the earliest works in the collection, most of them from a single evening in February 2021, and they are built from loose, looping colored line on bright grounds.
One room. The related greeting GM hangs in Occasions and Figures in the Other nnxyz wing.
wings.attribution: Works by Scrimshaw (scrimshaw.eth); attribution is retained on every page.
